info.title: ONE ICTMS API
info.description: ONE ICTMS Laravel API: registration, email and login OTP, password recovery, and JWT authentication stored in an HttpOnly cookie for browser clients. Redis stores OTP challenges and revoked JWT state. Browser authentication routes use Laravel web middleware for session-backed CSRF protection. The URL base /api plus paths /v1/auth/* yields /api/v1/auth/*. Browser POST endpoints require Laravel CSRF session cookies and a corresponding X-XSRF-TOKEN header; Bearer clients using the same web-protected routes also need CSRF unless routed separately. Library APIs provide Department, Division, and Position lists and authenticated administrative CRUD. Library view/update/delete IDs are supplied in JSON request bodies, never in URL paths. Mutating operations require appropriate administrative authorization before production deployment. System Registry API provides authenticated portfolio CRUD for system profiles, technology stacks, stakeholders, documents, and Git repository metadata. Registry IDs are supplied in JSON request bodies rather than URL paths. Registry schema updated for RegistryDesc, nullable Department-linked managing office, Department-linked business owner, and Library-linked numeric reference IDs. Includes seven Registry Library groups (Development Type, Managing Type, Development Solution Type, Stakeholder Type, Document Type, Registry Status, and Tech Stack), each with five CRUD endpoints. List APIs expose active values; protected mutations use JSON bodies.

get.description: Returns a success response when the API is running. No authentication is required. This endpoint does not check database or mail service connectivity.

Call before browser POST requests. Under the Laravel web middleware, initializes the CSRF session and returns Laravel session and XSRF-TOKEN cookies. The frontend must retain cookies (same-origin proxy recommended) and send X-XSRF-TOKEN on subsequent unsafe methods. Does not authenticate the user or issue a JWT.

get.description: Reads JWT from HttpOnly cookie (or Bearer header when applicable), checks JWT validity, Redis blacklist and token_version middleware, then returns the authenticated user and loaded details. Organization objects are optional and depend on the AuthResource implementation. Browser clients authenticate automatically through the HttpOnly ictms_access_token cookie; Swagger Authorize is only needed for Bearer-token clients.

403.description: Access denied (including revoked token-version policy, depending on middleware).

Set-Cookie.description: Expire the HttpOnly JWT cookie with the same path/domain used at issuance.
